subject: POC plan & integration checklist for Quantify.ai — next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@quantify.ai>, Liz Chen <liz@quantify.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC plan & integration checklist for Quantify.ai — next steps

Hi Samir / Liz —

Thanks again for the productive call today. This thread is a short recap and a proposed minimal POC plan so we can start engineering work next week. Please reply with any edits, ownership changes, or timing constraints.

High-level goal
- Validate Redwood inference for your real-time anomaly detection pipeline (50 QPS ingest, median latency < 120ms at 512 tokens, cost < $0.0009/token with quantized model)

Proposed success criteria (sensors for pass/fail)
- Functional: model outputs match your evaluation set F1 >= 0.82 for anomaly labels
- Performance: 95th percentile latency under 200ms for 512-token rolling window at sustained 50 QPS in our Dedicated trial environment
- Operational: end-to-end integration with your streaming pipeline using our SDK with automated retry/backpressure and at least one tool-calling route exercised (webhook notification)

POC scope & timeline (week-by-week)
- Week 0 (this week): sign MPA (mutual action plan) + grant test account access (Samir)
- Week 1: SDK + API baseline integration (connect pipeline -> /v1/generate; enable streaming via SSE), quick smoke tests
- Week 2: Run 50 QPS load tests with KV/prefix caching enabled; iterate on batching/quantization profile
- Week 3: Quality evaluation on your holdout set; finalize SLA targets for pilot

Ownership
- Quantify.ai: provide data slices, holdout eval set, and point-of-contact for infra (Samir)
- Redwood: integration guide, SDK support (Dylan), scoped Dedicated trial capacity, and weekly checkpoints (Grace)

Immediate asks
1) Samir: confirm POC contact for infra and whether you need private VPC or hosted Dedicated trial
2) Liz: share the small holdout eval CSV and a sample streaming payload (redacted)
3) Everyone: confirm that the success criteria above match expectations or propose edits by EOD Thu

Attachments: draft milestone workbook attached (quantify-poc-milestones.xlsx) and a short SDK integration note (redwood-sdk-integration-guidance.pdf).

Cheers,
Grace

Subject: Re: POC plan & integration checklist for Quantify.ai — next steps

Thanks Grace — big +1 on the structure. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Ownership: I'll be the infra POC, Liz will own the evaluation set and metrics reporting.
2) Environment: we prefer a hosted Dedicated trial (no VPC) for quicker onboarding, but we need IP allowlisting for our upstream collectors.
3) Eval set: Liz will share a ~5k-record holdout CSV by Thu EOD (anonymized events). Will that be sufficient for calculating F1?

Technical notes / asks for Redwood
- SDK: we plan to integrate via your Python SDK; can you confirm support for streaming responses (SSE) and function-based tool calls (we need to forward to our alerting webhook when an anomaly is detected)?
- API routes: we expect to call POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-medium-quant to start; is there a recommended batching policy or default concurrency knob we should tune?

Timing: target start Monday 21 Jun. Is that feasible for your team?

Samir

Subject: Re: POC plan & integration checklist for Quantify.ai — next steps

Grace — quick technical confirmation:
- Python SDK: supports streaming via SSE and an async iterator (we return chunked tokens and final metadata). Example snippet in the attached PDF.
- Tool calling: function-style payloads are supported; you can map model outputs to a webhook POST for your alerting service. We recommend using idempotency keys on webhook calls and our built-in backoff policy for retries.
- Recommended default: start with request_concurrency=8 and batching_window_ms=30 for 50 QPS; switch to request_concurrency=16 for peak runs and enable prefix KV caching once you see stable latencies.

I'll own SDK troubleshooting during the POC. Karthik — can you prep the Dedicated trial instance and confirm the IP allowlist controls?

- Dylan
Senior SDK Engineer | Redwood Inference

Samir / Liz — great, thanks for the quick replies and confirmers. Two concrete next steps so we can hit the 21 Jun start target:

1) Sign the attached Mutual Action Plan (DocuSign link below) — this authorizes trial capacity and the test account. We need this signed by EOD Mon to reserve Dedicated pool for the first two weeks.
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/packets/ABCD-1234

2) Liz: please upload the anonymized holdout CSV to the shared Drive link and include a short README describing labels. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Quantify/POC-plan

Technical kickoff checklist (for engineering) — Dylan/Karthik, please confirm when done:
- [ ] Dedicated trial instance created and IP allowlist rule available (Karthik)
- [ ] SDK sample repo forked for Quantify with streaming example (Dylan)
- [ ] Initial /v1/generate integration validated (smoke tests)
- [ ] Function-call mapping set up to forward anomaly events to Quantify webhook (we'll use header x-qntfy-id for idempotency)

Final notes on integrations:
- Streaming: use SSE endpoint in SDK for token-level progress; set batching_window_ms low (15–30ms) during warmup then tune to 30–50ms for throughput/cost tradeoff
- Tool calling: use function signature schema; Redwood will return a fields object and a tool_call payload you can POST to your internal webhook. Include signing header per the guide.
- Metrics: we'll export per-route token latency and token cost to your console; we'll also ship a small Prometheus exporter if you want to pull metrics into your stack.

Attached: milestone workbook and SDK integration note (quantify-poc-milestones.xlsx, redwood-sdk-integration-guidance.pdf).

If you confirm the sign + upload today, we will schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff for Mon 21 Jun 10:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
